text: Movies lied about quicksand. It can't swallow you.
What actually happens if you step in quicksand, and how do you survive it?
But it can still kill you.
You step onto wet, shiny sand.
Your foot sinks. Then the other.
In real life, quicksand is twice as dense as you.
So you float, waist-deep. Then you stop.
The water drains out. The sand locks around your legs.
Yanking a foot out takes car-lifting force.
The sun beats down. You're thirsty. Your legs cramp.
Your heart pounds. Behind you, the tide returns.
That's what kills people. Not the sand. The water.
So how do you escape? Don't pull.
Lean back and spread your arms like floating in a pool.
Wiggle your legs in slow, tiny circles.
Water seeps in, sand loosens, roll to solid ground.
So next time a movie swallows someone, remember:…
